page: Amazon Web Services c7i.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by the 4th Generation Intel Xeon Platinum 8488C processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture at a base clock speed of 3.2 GHz, the system provides 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity is configured at 128.0 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 5 GHz, delivering a compute-oriented ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The hardware integrates 105 MB of L3 cache, along with specialized vector and matrix instruction extensions including AVX-512, Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions with BF16 and INT8), and hardware cryptography accelerators like AES-NI and VAES.

The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage, meaning that storage-dependent workflows must rely entirely on remote network-attached Elastic Block Store volumes. For networking, the instance provisions a baseline throughput of 25 Gbps. Hardware acceleration is limited to CPU-native instruction blocks, as no discrete GPU is bundled with this instance type.

Benchmark results show top-quartile performance across diverse compute and memory-intensive metrics. The instance records strong figures in Geekbench multi-core (17,805.0) and single-core (1,950.0) tests, as well as software compilation (44,226.0) and PassMark CPU evaluations (70,832.71). Support for Intel AMX is evident in CPU-based LLM inference scores, achieving 2,617.76 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 135M model and 247.69 tokens per second on a 7B model. Similarly, in-memory throughput metrics highlight strong throughput, evidenced by 72.7 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 70.64 GB/s in static web serving throughput.

Because the 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides dense compute capability without the overhead of surplus RAM allocations, the server delivers high cost efficiency for CPU-bound tasks. Tradeoffs include the total absence of local scratch storage and low memory availability relative to core count. Workload profiles that align best with the c7i.16xlarge include compute-intensive batch processing, CI/CD code compilation, high-concurrency web serving, distributed caching layers, and CPU-driven machine learning inference.
description: Amazon Web Services c7i.16xlarge is a compute-optimized Nitro-based server featuring an Intel Xeon Platinum 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 64 dedicated vCPUs (32 physical cores), 128.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 5 GHz, and a 25 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance includes hardware support for Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions, but does not bundle local disk storage or discrete GPUs. Across synthetic and real-world benchmarks, the instance demonstrates upper-tier performance in multi-threaded compilation, PassMark CPU tests, Redis operations, and CPU-based LLM inference. Its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM balance ensures resource efficiency for compute-dense applications without paying for unneeded memory overhead. Best-fit workloads include CI/CD build environments, batch processing pipelines, web serving fleets, distributed caches, and CPU-centric model inference.
